exact_statement: For each system g, score only non-elemental target candidates T_g from a finite phase panel; elemental reference phases remain competitors. Let d_gi be the signed target-removed hull margin and d_hat_gi its prediction. If the frozen predictor, candidate generator, panel rule, and delta do not use calibration/test reference labels, and the n calibration systems plus one future system are exchangeable as whole groups, the split-conformal order statistic q_delta of S_g=max_{i in T_g}|d_gi-d_hat_gi| gives Pr(max_{i in T_new}|d_new,i-d_hat_new,i| <= q_delta) >= 1-delta. Every candidate with d_hat_i+q_delta<=0 is simultaneously stable relative to that declared phase panel at marginal system-level coverage; every candidate with d_hat_i-q_delta>0 is simultaneously unstable relative to that panel.
assumptions: Same named energy/free-energy target, pressure, temperature, reference convention, and phase-panel protocol in calibration and test systems.
Predictor fitting, model selection, candidate generation, phase-panel rule, and delta are fixed without using calibration or test reference labels.
Calibration and future chemical systems are exchangeable as whole groups under the frozen procedure.
For global stability claims, each phase panel includes every admissible competing phase; otherwise the certificate is panel-relative only.
Calibration reference energies target the named model or physical observable; DFT labels certify DFT, not nature.
Targets are non-elemental candidates with a feasible mass-balanced competitor mixture; elemental references are present as competitors.
novelty_boundary: No priority claim. This is a direct application of group-maximum split conformal calibration to convex-hull margins; hull-aware Bayesian active learning already exists. The possible new contribution would be empirical demonstration of useful whole-system coverage and efficiency, which has not been done here.

costs.acquisition: Whole-system calibration requires reference energies for the phases needed to construct the true panel hull in each calibration system; at least 19 groups are needed for a finite 95% split-conformal order statistic.
costs.runtime: For m phases and q components, construct margins by convex-hull or LP methods; then sort n scalar calibration scores in O(n log n). High-fidelity phase energies and structure enumeration dominate.
costs.model_boundary: Coverage does not address ungenerated structures or finite-temperature corrections unless they are included in panel and reference target.

falsifier: On exchangeability-credible held-out complete chemical systems, observed simultaneous panel-level coverage is below 1-delta; or at equal high-fidelity energy budget the method yields no more certified candidates than phasewise conformal intervals plus robust hull LP.
next_gate: Run a preregistered leave-one-chemical-system-out/whole-system calibration study with a frozen seven-facet or graph-energy predictor, same candidate panel, and PBE/r2SCAN (then experimental where available) labels; compare nominal hull, phasewise conformal plus LP, group-margin conformal, and CAL under matched DFT budgets.

exact_statement: If phase-energy error has form e_j-e_hat_j=x_j^T beta+r_j and a decomposition satisfies x_i=sum_j lambda_j x_j, then the decomposition-energy error is exactly r_i-sum_j lambda_j r_j; an arbitrary shared composition-linear offset beta cancels. If |r_j|<=epsilon for every relevant phase, the signed hull-margin error is at most 2 epsilon.
assumptions: Composition vectors are normalized on the same per-atom basis and obey exact element balance.
The nuisance beta is shared across the target and all competing phases in the same chemical system.
The residual bound is simultaneous over the full declared phase panel.
novelty_boundary: Mass-balance cancellation is standard reaction thermodynamics; no novelty or priority claim. The useful refinement is to calibrate reaction/hull-margin residuals instead of treating marginal formation-energy MAE as the certificate quantity.

costs.acquisition: Need simultaneous non-affine residual bounds or a held-out reaction-margin calibration distribution; absolute energy MAE is insufficient.
costs.runtime: No additional cost once energy residual bounds and hull LP inputs are supplied.

falsifier: Held-out phase errors are not well described by a shared affine composition component plus small residual, or reaction-margin calibration fails to improve on phasewise calibration at matched coverage.
next_gate: Measure reaction-balanced residuals for competing decomposition reactions across whole held-out chemical systems and test whether calibration intervals shrink while retaining simultaneous coverage.

exact_statement: For a fixed finite phase panel with independent residual intervals r_j in [a_j,b_j] after an arbitrary shared affine composition error, target i is robustly stable iff h_i+b_i <= min_{lambda in Lambda_i} sum_j lambda_j(h_j+a_j); it is robustly unstable iff h_i+a_i > min_{lambda in Lambda_i} sum_j lambda_j(h_j+b_j). Both tests reduce to linear programs; all other cases are UNKNOWN.
assumptions: The uncertainty set is a Cartesian box for residual errors, with nonnegative mixture weights and mass balance.
The competitor panel is finite and specified.
LP values are certified to sufficient numeric precision; exact rational data can use exact LP certificates.
novelty_boundary: This is standard robust optimization applied to the standard phase-hull LP, not a novel algorithm and not a nature-level guarantee.

costs.acquisition: Residual intervals must cover every relevant competing phase simultaneously.
costs.runtime: One rational LP per candidate per status test; polynomial in panel size and encoded input length, aside from structure generation and energy acquisition.

falsifier: An LP primal/dual witness violates the claimed inequality or a test with energies inside the stated intervals contradicts the robust label.
next_gate: Implement a rational/interval-certified LP verifier if this is retained for a future application; no implementation is claimed in this branch.

exact_statement: A stable certificate over an enumerated finite phase panel does not imply stability against all possible phases. Binary endpoint phases A,B at zero energy and target AB at -0.10 eV/atom produce a stable target in the panel; an omitted A2B phase at composition x_B=1/3 and energy -0.30 eV/atom yields a mass-balanced mixture at x_B=1/2 with energy -0.225 eV/atom, rendering AB unstable.
assumptions: No lower energy bound or exhaustive enumeration is supplied for omitted phases.
novelty_boundary: Elementary but load-bearing scope boundary; GNoME and the 2026 seven-facet preprint also state discoveries are relative to known/declared phase sets and that structure search remains unresolved.

costs.acquisition: Global certification needs exhaustive structure/composition search or a valid lower bound for every omitted phase; that cost is not supplied by the finite-panel LP.
costs.runtime: The finite-panel LP can be cheap compared with the unbounded structure search.

falsifier: A claimed global certificate supplies a verifiable lower bound covering all omitted admissible phases; then this counterexample no longer applies to that enlarged interface.
next_gate: Keep all reports explicitly panel-relative until an independently checkable structure-space lower bound is available.

exact_statement: The June 2026 v2 preprint titled A geometric basis for materials families in inorganic solids reports a 7-facet max-affine surrogate with 0.076 eV/atom test MAE on a random 20% split of 51,068 one-lowest-structure-per-composition entries restricted to one-to-five elements and within 0.025 eV/atom of the Materials Project hull; it states more facets would be needed to reproduce the exact hull and its composition-only method does not remove the structure-search problem.
assumptions: Statement is reported preprint evidence, not independent reproduction or experimental validation.
Random compound-level split and DFT labels are the scope of the reported test.
novelty_boundary: A 76 meV/atom MAE is an average prediction statistic, not a simultaneous error bound on balanced decomposition margins and not a certificate for systems outside a random split.

costs.acquisition: Training corpus of 51,068 near-hull structure/composition records; actual structure generation/evaluation remains.
costs.runtime: Reported method is a fitted shallow max-affine model; candidate structure search and any higher-fidelity labels add separate cost.

falsifier: Primary v2 paper text or code contradicts any listed split, dataset filter, MAE, or stated structure-search limitation.
next_gate: Evaluate whole-system held-out reaction-margin coverage; do not infer certificate quality from formation-energy MAE.
